learning_objective: 🌍 Understand what makes an organism 'living', explore Earth's incredible biodiversity, and learn how scientists name and classify every creature!

नामकरण (जीवों को वैज्ञानिक नाम देने की प्रक्रिया)

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Living things grow, reproduce, sense their environment, and have metabolism. However, growth and reproduction are not 'defining' properties (non-living mountains grow by accumulation, and mules cannot reproduce). Metabolism and cellular organization are the true defining features of life.

Introduced by Carolus Linnaeus, it is a universally accepted naming system. Every organism gets a two-part Latin name: the Genus (capitalized) and the specific epithet (lowercase). Example: Homo sapiens (Human) or Mangifera indica (Mango).
Organisms are classified into a step-by-step hierarchy. Remember the order from largest to smallest: Kingdom -> Phylum (or Division for plants) -> Class -> Order -> Family -> Genus -> Species.

Tools that help in identifying and studying organisms. These include Herbaria (dried plant sheets), Botanical Gardens (live plants), Museums (preserved plant and animal specimens), and Zoological Parks (wild animals in captivity).
An analytical tool used to identify plants and animals based on their similarities and differences. It usually relies on contrasting characters, often in a pair called a 'couplet'.

fun_activity.title: 🏷️ Name That Species
fun_activity.instructions: Scientific names often tell you something about the organism! 'Mangifera indica' tells you the mango is from India. 'Felis catus' is the domestic cat. Look up the scientific name of your favorite animal and try to figure out what the Latin words mean!

exam_tips: 📌 Always underline scientific names when hand-writing them (e.g., _Mangifera_ _indica_). The genus name starts with a capital letter, and the species name starts with a small letter.
📌 'Species' is the lowest and most basic unit of classification, possessing the maximum number of common characteristics.
📌 ICBN stands for International Code for Botanical Nomenclature, and ICZN stands for Zoological Nomenclature.
quick_recap: ⭐ Cellular organization and consciousness are defining properties of living organisms.
⭐ Carolus Linnaeus is known as the Father of Taxonomy.
⭐ A 'Flora' contains the actual account of habitat and distribution of plants of a given area.
